subject: Social Media
title: Eyeballs as Revenue
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Eyeballs as Revenue.

hook.text: Google earns $300 billion yearly. Its product isn't search—it's your gaze. Advertisers pay per eyeball.

buildup.text: TV sold attention first. A 30-second Super Bowl ad costs $7 million because 100 million people watch.

discovery.text: Digital ads refined the model. Platforms track exactly what you see, how long, and what you click next.

twist.text: You pay nothing for most apps. That's because you're not the customer. You're the product being sold.

climax.text: The ad model means platforms want maximum time on screen. Your boredom is their lost revenue.

punchline.text: Free apps aren't free. You pay with your attention.

quiz.question: In the attention economy, what is the user to a free platform?
